hypothesis: The v005 breakout premise, sized by inverse volatility instead of equal capital and held to a breadth standard, turns a single-coin result into a portfolio result: positive net expectancy whose symbol-clustered confidence interval clears zero, spread over many coins, in both Bitcoin regimes.
rulesChosenFrom: The recorded failure modes of the versions before it, not from v011 data. v005 (243 trades, 33.7% win rate, +1.53% per trade) had a confidence interval of -2.9% to +6.3% and was flat without one coin: ZEC rose 24.7x and carried the result. v006 repeated v005 on a wider universe and produced the same trades. v009 and v010 asked for breadth (profitable pairs) and failed it. v011 changes two things and nothing else: position size is inverse-volatility with a per-coin cap rather than an equal slot, and the acceptance standard adds breadth, concentration and regime splits. No period is clean for these rules, so no historical test is claimed; the judgement window opens at the freeze.
survivorshipNote: The universe is held identical to v005 so the two versions answer the same question. It still includes pairs that were later delisted (EOS, MATIC); their history simply ends.

sizing.note: Each open position is weighted by 1/volatility over 60 days, scaled so the book targets 20% annualized volatility, then capped at 8% of book per coin and 100% gross. Cash is not borrowed and not reinvested.

execution: Signal on the daily close (00:00 UTC); fill at the next day's open. One position per symbol, long only. Weights are recomputed at each daily close and applied to the open, never inside the day.

judging.note: Judged on live paper signals only. The first verdict cannot be issued before the window closes, and a passing verdict needs the trade count, not just the calendar.

acceptance.regimes: every BTC up/down segment inside the judgement window, split on the 100-day SMA the strategy itself uses

dependability.note: A record older than this is reported as STALE. The strategy is not allowed to look flat when the engine is simply not running.

noRetuning: A failed verdict is published as a null and the version is retired. Any successor gets a new version number, new rules and a fresh window; the parameters above are never edited after the freeze.
retirement: A verdict of fail on any gate reason, published in full.
Seven consecutive days with no engine heartbeat.
Any published signal that cannot be reproduced from the frozen rules and the recorded bars.
